correctness.rationale: From the actual E(K_n) multiplication, x²=x iff each x_i satisfies x_i²+x_i=S with S=sum x_j². Common monic quadratic gives at most two coordinate values. For k selected u positions, v=-1-u, the exact equation (n−1)u²+(2(n−k)−1)u+(n−k)=0 has discriminant 1−4k(n−k). If p∤(n−1) there are 1+χ roots minus the coincident u=−1/2 precisely when p|(n+1); if p|(n−1) the equation is linear and solvable exactly when p∤(2k−1). Every nonconstant vector is double-represented by complementary marked sets, proving the half-sum and c0 constants. All roots have degree ≤2 over F_p, hence q^m parity pattern and zeta formula. Independently enumerated x²=x in 12 small (p,n) cases; examples (3,3):2 and (3,4):5 agree. Finite enumerations corroborate, not replace, all-n proof.

value.rationale: Individual idempotent elements of the canonical complete-graph evolution algebra are natural solutions of a quadratic dynamical fixed-point problem. The exact all-n odd-finite-field count, singular-adjacency characteristic branch, common splitting extension and Hasse–Weil-type point-counting zeta constitute a reusable exact arithmetic invariant, not a renaming of the algebra-automorphism problem. The result resolves an unlimited natural family, not an arbitrary tiny case.
